tools.name: create_upload_link
tools.description: Relay a file of any size up to 100 MB. Save the file to local disk first, call this with its path, then run the returned curl command in your shell to upload it. tools.name: relay_attached_file
tools.description: ChatGPT only: relay a file from the conversation (the host passes it as a file reference) and get a temporary download link.

tools.name: get_file_info
tools.description: Look up a relayed file by id or download URL: name, size, type, expiry and download link.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a relayed file's content (up to 1 MB) so an agent can pick up a file someone else relayed. Text comes back as text, images as images, other files as base64.

tools.name: delete_file
tools.description: Delete a relayed file before it expires. Requires the delete_token returned at upload.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "read_file" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_file_info · Private data: create_upload_link, relay_attached_file, get_file_info, read_file, delete_file · Public sink: create_upload_link, delete_file · Destructive: create_upload_link, delete_file.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_file_info · Private data: create_upload_link, relay_attached_file, get_file_info, read_file, delete_file · Public sink: create_upload_link, delete_file · Destructive: create_upload_link, delete_file

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
